lessons.title: Removing components the right way
lessons.html:
Plan before you pull

Removing a part sounds simple, but careless removal breaks bolts, damages parts and loses small pieces. Good removal makes the installation easy.

Before you start

  1. Read the job card and the workshop manual for the steps.
  2. Make the tractor safe: on level ground, implements down, key out, wheels chocked.
  3. Let the engine and oil cool.
  4. Get the right tools, drip trays, containers and labels ready.
  5. Clean the area around the part so dirt does not fall into openings.

During removal

  • Drain fluids first into clean drip trays if the part holds oil, coolant or fuel.
  • Take photos with your phone before you remove things, so you remember how hoses, wires and brackets fit.
  • Label wires, hoses and pipes with tape and a marker.
  • Cap or plug open hoses and ports to keep dirt out.
  • Keep bolts in order: put them in labelled bags or a tray, or push them back into their holes.
  • Support heavy parts with a jack, crane or helper before taking the last bolts out.

Stuck bolts and parts

Spray penetrating oil and wait. Use a six-point socket or ring spanner. Tap the bolt head gently to break rust. Do not use heat near fuel, hydraulic lines or rubber parts unless your supervisor allows it. Use a puller for gears, pulleys and bearings; do not hammer them off.

Inspect as you go

Look at the parts you remove. Note wear, cracks, broken teeth or leaks and tell the mechanic. This helps find why the part failed.

lessons.title: Installing components correctly
lessons.html:
Clean, check, fit, tighten, test

Installing a part properly is as important as the part itself. A new water pump will leak if the gasket is fitted wrongly.

Prepare

  • Check the new part is the correct one: compare part numbers and shape with the old part.
  • Clean mating surfaces. Scrape old gasket material off carefully without scratching. Do not let it fall into the engine.
  • Check threads are clean. Run a tap or die through damaged threads if allowed.
  • Use new gaskets, seals, O-rings and locking devices such as split pins and lock washers.

Fit

  1. Lightly oil O-rings and seals with the same fluid they will hold, unless the manual says otherwise.
  2. Line up the part. Never force it into place. If it does not fit, stop and check.
  3. Start all bolts by hand first so they do not cross-thread.
  4. Tighten in the sequence the manual shows, often a crisscross pattern, in stages.
  5. Use a torque wrench for the final tightness from the manual.
  6. Fit locking devices.

Reconnect and refill

Reconnect hoses, wires and pipes using your photos and labels. Remove all caps and plugs. Refill fluids to the correct level with the correct type. Bleed air from fuel or hydraulic systems if needed.

Test

  • Check that no tools or rags are left in the engine bay.
  • Start the engine and check for leaks, noises and warning lights.
  • Check fluid levels again after running.
  • Test the system works, for example the hitch lifts or the pump circulates coolant.

Record

Write on the job card what you removed and fitted, part numbers and any problems you saw. Put old parts where the supervisor says, as the customer may want to see them.

Key points

  • Read the manual and make the tractor safe before starting.
  • Photograph, label and cap everything you disconnect.
  • Support heavy parts before removing the last bolts.
  • Use new seals and gaskets and start bolts by hand.
  • Torque to the manual, refill, check for leaks and record the work.
